title: Choosing the right hamster species
steps: Research whether you are keeping a Syrian, dwarf or Chinese hamster.
Check species-specific housing, diet and handling requirements before buying equipment.
Plan for one hamster per enclosure.
caution: Hamsters are generally solitary; cohabitation can lead to serious fighting.

title: Why hamsters live alone
steps: House each pet hamster separately in a secure enclosure.
Provide individual wheels, food and hiding places.
Watch for signs of stress if a hamster has previously been housed with others.
caution: Do not introduce unfamiliar hamsters to share a cage.

title: Choosing a spacious enclosure
steps: Prioritise generous continuous floor space rather than multiple tiny levels.
Use a secure, well-ventilated enclosure with a deep substrate base.
Check current welfare guidance for suitable minimum dimensions for your species.
caution: Small modular cages and tubes are often unsuitable as primary homes.

title: Secure enclosure lids
steps: Check lid clips, hinges and mesh for gaps.
Keep tall furnishings away from openings.
Test that the enclosure closes securely after cleaning.
caution: Hamsters can squeeze through surprisingly small gaps.

title: Deep bedding for burrowing
steps: Provide a generous depth of safe, low-dust bedding that can hold tunnels.
Allow the hamster to build burrows without frequent disturbance.
Top up bedding gently as needed.
caution: Avoid scented bedding and fluffy cotton nesting material.

title: Safe paper bedding
steps: Choose unscented, low-dust paper-based bedding.
Check that it is absorbent and suitable for burrowing.
Remove soiled areas without destroying the whole nest.
caution: Avoid products with strong fragrances or added deodorisers.

title: Avoiding unsafe nesting fluff
steps: Offer plain unscented toilet tissue or suitable paper nesting material.
Let the hamster carry and arrange it.
Remove any stringy or fibrous products from the enclosure.
caution: Cotton wool and similar fluffy fibres can entangle limbs or cause problems if swallowed.

title: Building a multi-chamber hide
steps: Provide a dark, secure hide large enough for the hamster to turn around.
Offer multiple chambers or additional shelters.
Keep at least one hide near the deepest bedding area.
caution: Avoid small entrances that may trap a hamster with full cheek pouches.

title: Choosing a safe running wheel
steps: Choose a solid-surface wheel large enough for a straight-backed running posture.
Make sure the wheel spins freely and remains stable.
Inspect for cracks, sharp edges and trapped bedding.
caution: Avoid wire or mesh running surfaces and wheels that force the back to curve.

title: Wheel placement and stability
steps: Position the wheel on a secure platform above deep bedding.
Check that it cannot tip into burrows.
Clean accumulated debris from the running surface.
caution: A falling wheel can collapse tunnels or injure a hamster.

title: Providing a sand bath
steps: Use a suitable dust-free hamster-safe sand in a sturdy shallow container.
Allow the hamster to roll and groom naturally.
Sift soiled areas and replace dirty sand.
caution: Avoid fine chinchilla dust and perfumed bath products.

title: Why hamsters should not be bathed
steps: Offer a sand bath for normal coat maintenance.
If fur is soiled, identify the cause and ask a vet about safe spot cleaning.
Keep the enclosure dry and clean.
caution: Water baths can cause stress and chilling; never use household shampoo.

title: Safe enclosure temperature
steps: Keep the enclosure in a stable indoor room away from direct sun and radiators.
Check for draughts and overheating.
Provide ample nesting material for normal comfort.
caution: Extreme cold or heat can be dangerous; a cold unresponsive hamster needs urgent veterinary advice.

title: Quiet daytime resting
steps: Place the enclosure in a calm area away from loud music and daytime disturbance.
Allow uninterrupted sleep during daylight hours.
Plan interaction for when the hamster wakes naturally.
caution: Repeated waking can cause stress and defensive biting.

title: Understanding nocturnal activity
steps: Expect most activity in the evening and overnight.
Observe food gathering, digging and wheel use when awake.
Keep a consistent routine around natural activity times.
caution: A hamster sleeping through the day is usually normal.

title: Reading hamster body language
steps: Watch for freezing, flattening, squeaking or frantic attempts to escape.
Stop handling when the hamster seems frightened.
Offer a retreat to a familiar hide.
caution: Biting may be a fear response, not misbehaviour.

title: Gentle first-day settling
steps: Set up the enclosure fully before bringing the hamster home.
Allow several quiet days to settle with minimal disturbance.
Offer food and water without forcing interaction.
caution: Avoid lifting a newly arrived hamster before it feels secure.

title: Hand-taming with treats
steps: Offer a tiny suitable treat on an open palm while the hamster is awake.
Let it approach and step onto your hand voluntarily.
Practise short calm sessions close to the floor.
caution: Never chase, grab or wake a hamster to tame it.

title: Safe lifting and carrying
steps: Scoop gently with both hands or use a familiar mug or tunnel.
Keep the hamster low over a secure surface.
Return it promptly if it struggles.
caution: Hamsters can jump suddenly and be seriously injured by falls.

title: Handling with children
steps: Supervise children closely and teach them to stay seated during handling.
Let the hamster approach rather than forcing contact.
Wash hands after handling and cleaning.
caution: Hamsters are delicate and may bite when startled.

title: Playpen exercise sessions
steps: Use a secure escape-proof playpen with familiar hides and toys.
Supervise the hamster throughout the session.
Return it to the enclosure before it becomes stressed.
caution: Never leave a hamster loose near cables, furniture gaps or other pets.

title: Avoiding exercise balls
steps: Provide a suitable wheel and supervised playpen instead.
Offer tunnels, boxes and safe exploration objects.
Let the hamster choose when to explore.
caution: Exercise balls restrict control and ventilation and can cause injury or stress.

title: Cardboard tunnels and hides
steps: Offer clean plain cardboard tubes or boxes without staples or tape.
Cut larger openings for a Syrian hamster.
Replace items when chewed or soiled.
caution: Check openings carefully to prevent entrapment.

title: Scatter feeding for enrichment
steps: Sprinkle part of the normal food ration around safe bedding.
Allow the hamster to forage and store food.
Check that hidden fresh food does not spoil.
caution: Scatter feeding should not increase the total daily ration.

title: Dig boxes and substrates
steps: Provide a separate dig area with an appropriate hamster-safe substrate.
Offer varied textures such as safe paper bedding or suitable coco soil.
Keep the area dry and check for mould.
caution: Do not use garden soil containing fertilisers or pesticides.

title: Safe chew materials
steps: Offer untreated hamster-safe wood chews or appropriate cardboard.
Inspect toys for splinters, glue and loose parts.
Replace damaged items promptly.
caution: Avoid painted or chemically treated wood.

title: Choosing a balanced staple food
steps: Select a complete hamster food suitable for the species.
Follow the manufacturer's feeding guide and monitor body condition.
Use treats sparingly alongside the staple diet.
caution: Dwarf hamsters may have different dietary considerations; ask a knowledgeable vet.

title: Fresh water every day
steps: Provide clean drinking water in a suitable bottle or stable shallow bowl.
Check that the bottle spout works and the bowl is not buried.
Refresh and clean the container regularly.
caution: Lack of drinking water can quickly become serious.

title: Safe vegetable portions
steps: Offer tiny portions of suitable washed vegetables.
Introduce new foods one at a time.
Remove uneaten fresh food before it spoils.
caution: Large portions or sudden dietary changes may cause digestive upset.

title: Treats and sugary foods
steps: Keep treats small and infrequent.
Prefer appropriate species-safe options rather than sugary human snacks.
Monitor weight and food hoarding.
caution: Avoid chocolate, sweets and sticky sugary foods.

title: Foods to keep away
steps: Keep chocolate, alcohol, caffeine and seasoned human food out of reach.
Check the safety of unfamiliar fruit, vegetables and plants before offering them.
Store pet food away from household chemicals.
caution: Do not guess whether a food is safe; consult reliable species-specific guidance.

title: Protein in the diet
steps: Choose a nutritionally complete hamster mix containing suitable protein.
If offering extras, use only tiny species-appropriate portions.
Remove perishable food promptly.
caution: Do not substitute random high-protein snacks for a balanced staple diet.

title: Checking hidden food stores
steps: Inspect accessible hoards gently during spot cleaning.
Remove damp or mouldy food and old fresh produce.
Leave clean dry staple food stores where practical.
caution: Avoid repeatedly destroying the entire hoard, which can cause stress.

title: Spot cleaning without stress
steps: Remove wet bedding and obvious waste from toilet areas.
Leave clean nesting material and familiar scent where possible.
Replace only what is necessary with fresh safe bedding.
caution: Avoid stripping the entire enclosure unnecessarily.

title: Full enclosure refresh planning
steps: Plan a larger refresh only when hygiene requires it.
Retain some clean old bedding to preserve familiar scent.
Keep the hamster in a secure ventilated carrier during maintenance.
caution: Frequent total clean-outs can be stressful and disrupt burrows.

title: Cleaning the wheel and sand bath
steps: Wipe the wheel with a pet-safe method and dry fully.
Sift the sand bath and replace soiled sand.
Return equipment to familiar positions.
caution: Never leave strong cleaning-product residues on toys.

title: Cleaning food and water dishes
steps: Wash bowls and bottles with hot water and appropriate pet-safe methods.
Rinse thoroughly and dry.
Check bottles for leaks and blocked nozzles.
caution: Do not use strongly fragranced cleaners.

title: Recognising normal cheek pouch use
steps: Observe the hamster collecting and transporting food in its cheeks.
Allow it to empty pouches naturally in a quiet space.
Watch for persistent swelling or trouble eating.
caution: A pouch that stays swollen or appears infected needs veterinary attention.

title: Weekly weight monitoring
steps: Use a small digital scale and secure container.
Weigh at a similar time each week.
Record changes alongside appetite and activity.
caution: Unexpected weight loss can indicate illness and needs veterinary assessment.

title: Checking eyes and nose
steps: Observe whether eyes are clear and the nose is free of discharge.
Note squinting, crusting or noisy breathing.
Seek veterinary advice if symptoms appear.
caution: Do not apply human eye drops or medicines without a vet.

title: Checking teeth and chewing
steps: Watch the hamster eat and chew normally.
Offer safe chewing materials and appropriate food.
Seek veterinary care for drooling, difficulty eating or abnormal tooth growth.
caution: Do not attempt to trim teeth yourself.

title: Coat and skin checks
steps: Look for bald patches, redness, wounds or excessive scratching.
Review bedding and possible irritation.
Consult a vet if skin changes persist or worsen.
caution: Do not use flea products intended for dogs or cats.

title: When a hamster stops eating
steps: Check whether the hamster is awake and normally active.
Note any lack of food intake, droppings or water consumption.
Contact an exotic-pet vet promptly if appetite has stopped.
caution: Small animals can deteriorate quickly; do not wait days for improvement.

title: Diarrhoea and wet tail warning
steps: Check for wetness around the rear, diarrhoea, lethargy or poor appetite.
Keep the hamster warm and calm while arranging immediate veterinary help.
Clean the enclosure only as advised to avoid further stress.
caution: Wet tail and severe diarrhoea are emergencies, especially in young hamsters.

title: Breathing difficulties
steps: Watch for laboured breathing, clicking, discharge or unusual stillness.
Minimise stress and keep the environment comfortable.
Contact an exotic-pet vet urgently.
caution: Never give human cold medicines or antibiotics without veterinary direction.

title: Lumps and swellings
steps: Note the size, location and appearance of a lump.
Avoid squeezing or puncturing it.
Arrange a veterinary examination.
caution: Not all swellings are harmless; diagnosis requires a vet.

title: Caring for senior hamsters
steps: Make food and water easy to reach without climbing.
Provide soft accessible bedding and stable wheel access.
Monitor weight, grooming and movement more closely.
caution: New weakness or appetite changes should be assessed by a vet.

title: Preparing for a veterinary visit
steps: Locate an exotic-pet vet before an emergency happens.
Use a secure carrier with familiar bedding and ventilation.
Bring notes on food, symptoms, weight and housing.
caution: Avoid overheating or chilling during travel.

title: Travel and temporary care
steps: Arrange a reliable carer familiar with the hamster's nocturnal routine.
Leave written feeding, cleaning and emergency instructions.
Keep the enclosure secure and avoid unnecessary transport.
caution: Do not leave a hamster unattended for several days.

title: Escaped hamster search
steps: Close doors and remove other pets from the area.
Search quietly at dusk near walls, furniture and warm hiding places.
Place familiar bedding and a safe food lure in a secure humane capture setup.
caution: Never use glue traps or hazardous snap traps.

title: Emergency supplies checklist
steps: Keep a secure carrier, spare bedding, water container and vet contact details ready.
Maintain a backup food supply and a working thermometer.
Review the kit before holidays or moves.
caution: Emergency supplies do not replace prompt veterinary care.
